trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight KL lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Take the Amsterdam Airport Express (Sprinter) from Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal (~17 min, €5.40). Check in to Canal House Amsterdam and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Orientation Walk along the Jordaan neighborhood and the Prinsengracht canal. Stroll the iconic canal ring, admire 17th-century merchant houses, cross picturesque bridges, and get your bearings. Stop by the Noordermarkt square area. Totally free and a perfect soft introduction to Amsterdam.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Nine Streets (De 9 Straatjes) — a charming grid of boutique-lined canals perfect for an evening wander. Grab a budget-friendly Dutch stroopwafel or herring from a street stall (~€2–3).

meals.breakfast: Eat before or at Schiphol Airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Grab a broodje (Dutch sandwich) from a local bakery or Albert Heijn supermarket near Centraal Station (~€3–5).
meals.dinner: Moeders Restaurant or Winkel 43 area — try Dutch erwtensoep (split pea soup) or a simple stamppot at a brown café (bruine kroeg). Budget ~€12–16.

day_by_day.notes: Buy an OV-chipkaart (public transport card) at Schiphol or Centraal Station for easy tram/bus use throughout the trip. Load €20 to start. Canal House Amsterdam is ideally situated near the canal ring, making the afternoon walk easily walkable.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit — Open from 09:00. Arrive early to beat Saturday crowds. Explore masterpieces by Rembrandt (The Night Watch), Vermeer, and Dutch Golden Age artifacts. Budget ~2.5–3 hours. Admission: ~€22.50 (book online in advance to save time and sometimes get a small discount).
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum — Located just a 5-minute walk from the Rijksmuseum in Museumplein. Discover the world's largest Van Gogh collection including Sunflowers and The Bedroom. Book tickets online in advance (~€22). Spend 1.5–2 hours. Afterward, relax on the Museumplein lawn (free) and enjoy the open green space.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or tram back toward the canal belt. Explore Leidseplein square for its lively atmosphere. Browse the outdoor terraces and street performers.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh stroopwafels and coffee at Albert Heijn supermarket or a local bakery near the hotel (~€4–6).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or grab a sandwich/wrap from a Museumplein food cart or the Rijksmuseum café's grab-and-go section (~€6–8).
meals.dinner: Foodhallen Amsterdam (indoor food market on Bellamyplein) — wide variety of affordable global street food stalls, budget ~€10–14. Take Tram 1 or 7 from Leidseplein (~10 min).

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is busy at both museums — pre-booking timed entry tickets online is strongly recommended and often mandatory. Museumplein is a 20-minute walk or short tram ride (Tram 2 or 5) from the hotel area. Combo-ing both museums on one day maximizes your museum budget efficiently.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour — One of Amsterdam's most moving and historically significant sites. Book tickets well in advance online (often sells out weeks ahead, ~€16). The hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid during WWII is a deeply emotional experience. Allow 1.5–2 hours. Located on Prinsengracht, very close to Canal House Amsterdam.
day_by_day.afternoon: Canal Boat Tour — Depart from a nearby dock along Prinsengracht or Damrak. A guided canal boat tour (~€15–18 for a 1-hour tour with Lovers Canal Cruises or Blue Boat Company) takes you past the UNESCO-listed canal ring, 17th-century warehouses, and iconic houseboats. Alternatively, rent a pedal boat (~€14/hour) for a fun budget DIY option.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Dam Square and the Royal Palace (Koninklijk Paleis) exterior — free to admire outside, or enter for ~€12.50. Walk through the Kalverstraat shopping street and the Begijnhof, a serene hidden courtyard (free entry).

meals.breakfast: Noordermarkt Sunday Organic Market (open Sundays 09:00–15:00) — grab fresh fruit, cheese, and bread directly from vendors (~€5–7). A quintessential Amsterdam Sunday experience.
meals.lunch: Picnic along the Prinsengracht canal with market finds, or grab a Dutch pancake (pannenkoek) at Pancakes Amsterdam near the Anne Frank House (~€10–12).
meals.dinner: Soup en Zo (a beloved budget soup restaurant) or De Vliegende Schotel (vegetarian, affordable) near the Jordaan area. Budget ~€10–13.

day_by_day.notes: The Anne Frank House is within easy walking distance of Canal House Amsterdam (roughly 5–10 minutes on foot along the canal). Sunday morning at Noordermarkt is a beloved local ritual — arrive early for the best selection. Keep your OV-chipkaart handy for the tram to Dam Square.

day_by_day.morning: Amsterdam Museum of the Canals (Amsterdam Museum / Stadsarchief) or the free Scheepvaartmuseum (National Maritime Museum, ~€17.50) — dive deeper into Amsterdam's history as a global trading powerhouse. Alternatively, visit the Begijnhof and Amsterdam Historical Museum area around Spui square (partly free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Plantage neighborhood — visit Hortus Botanicus (one of the world's oldest botanical gardens, ~€11) and stroll past the Artis Zoo exterior. Walk along the Entrepotdok canal warehouse district, a beautifully preserved 19th-century docklands area (free). Cross over to the Eastern Docklands for modern architecture views.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through De Pijp neighborhood — Amsterdam's bohemian quarter. Explore the Albert Cuyp Market (open Mon–Sat, closes ~17:00 so catch the tail end) for cheap snacks, fresh produce, and local goods. Soak in the multicultural street life.

meals.breakfast: Café Brecht or a local brown café near the hotel for koffie verkeerd (Dutch latte) and a boterham (~€5–7).
meals.lunch: Albert Cuyp Market street food — try Dutch raw herring (haring) with onions (~€3–4), stroopwafels, or a fresh broodje from a stall (~€5–8 total).
meals.dinner: Warung Spang Makandra (Surinamese-Javanese cuisine, a De Pijp institution) — generous portions at very low prices, budget ~€9–13. Cash preferred.

day_by_day.notes: The Plantage and De Pijp neighborhoods are best reached by tram (lines 9 and 24 respectively from the city center). Both areas are off the typical tourist trail and offer an authentic Amsterdam experience. Monday is generally less crowded at most attractions.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning free exploration — revisit a favorite canal street or neighborhood. Visit the Westerkerk (Westerkerk church, free entry or small donation) near the Anne Frank House for panoramic tower views (~€9 to climb the tower). Browse independent bookshops and vintage stores along Haarlemmerdijk street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Amsterdam Centraal area for last-minute souvenir shopping at budget-friendly spots (avoid tourist trap shops — try the Waterlooplein Flea Market, open Mon–Sat, for unique affordable finds). Walk across the IJ waterfront and take the free GVB ferry behind Centraal Station to Amsterdam Noord for a quick, scenic, zero-cost boat ride with great city skyline views.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in the Jordaan neighborhood. Enjoy one final Dutch meal before departure preparations.

meals.breakfast: Full Dutch breakfast at the hotel if included, or visit Café 't Smalle (a historic Jordaan brown café) for coffee and apple cake (~€6–8).
meals.lunch: Grab a quick, cheap lunch at Broodje Bert or any local broodje shop near Waterlooplein (~€4–6).
meals.dinner: De Reiger (classic Dutch Jordaan brown café) or Café de Tuin — hearty Dutch dishes and local beers in an authentic setting. Budget ~€14–18 for a satisfying farewell meal.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your departure is in the evening (many hotels offer free luggage storage for the day). The free IJ ferry is a hidden gem — runs 24/7 and gives a wonderful perspective of the city from the water at zero cost. Allow at least 45–60 minutes to get to Schiphol from Centraal Station by train.

trip_options.title: Classic Amsterdam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Rijksmuseum Visit
experiences.description: Explore the Netherlands' premier museum housing masterpieces by Rembrandt, Vermeer, and Van Gogh. Marvel at the famous Night Watch painting and centuries of Dutch Golden Age art and history across stunning gallery halls.

experiences.name: Anne Frank House Tour
experiences.description: Walk through the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid during World War II. A deeply moving and historically significant experience that brings one of history's most important stories to life. Book tickets well in advance online.

experiences.name: Canal Boat Tour

experiences.name: Van Gogh Museum

experiences.name: Jordaan Neighborhood Walking Tour & Dutch Food Tasting
experiences.description: Wander through Amsterdam's most picturesque neighborhood with a guided walking tour, exploring hidden courtyards (hofjes), independent galleries, and local markets. Sample traditional Dutch bites including stroopwafels, raw herring, and aged Gouda cheese along the way.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In: Flight KL lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Take the Amsterdam Airport Express train (Sprinter) from Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal (~17 min, €5), then a short taxi or tram to Canal House Amsterdam. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with a self-guided stroll along the Herengracht and Keizersgracht canals right outside your hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Canal Boat Tour: At ~15:00, join a guided Canal Boat Tour departing from nearby Centraal Station or the Leidseplein area. Cruise Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed canal ring, gliding past 17th-century merchant houses, narrow bridges, and the iconic canal belt. This is a perfect low-energy introduction to the city after a long flight (~75 min tour, approx. €18–22 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Jordaan Neighborhood Exploration: After the canal tour, walk into the charming Jordaan district — just minutes from most canal house hotels. Browse the boutiques, admire the hofjes (hidden courtyards), and soak in the golden-hour light on the canals. End the evening with a relaxed dinner at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and stroopwafel or a light snack at Schiphol Airport before landing — no formal breakfast scheduled.
meals.lunch: Quick and casual at Broodje Bert or a local broodjeszaak (Dutch sandwich shop) near the hotel after check-in (~€8–12). Try a classic uitsmijter (open-faced egg sandwich).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Café de Reiger in the Jordaan — a beloved Dutch brasserie with seasonal menus and a cozy, authentic atmosphere. Budget ~€25–35 per person including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light and relaxed to recover from travel. The canal boat tour requires no advance booking but pre-booking online saves time and sometimes offers a small discount. Wear comfortable walking shoes from the start — Amsterdam's cobblestones are charming but uneven.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit: Arrive at opening time (9:00 AM) to beat the crowds at the Netherlands' premier museum. Spend 2.5–3 hours exploring masterpieces by Rembrandt (The Night Watch), Vermeer (The Milkmaid), and Delft blue collections. Pre-book tickets online (~€22.50 per person). The museum is a 10-minute tram ride from the canal house area (Tram 2 or 5 to Museumplein).
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum: Just a 5-minute walk from the Rijksmuseum, head to the Van Gogh Museum after a midday break. Discover the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's works including Sunflowers and The Bedroom. Allow 1.5–2 hours. Pre-book tickets (~€22 per person) as this museum regularly sells out. Afterward, relax in the Vondelpark nearby — Amsterdam's beloved green lung.
day_by_day.evening: Leidseplein & Dinner: Head to the lively Leidseplein square for dinner and drinks. Explore the bustling café terraces and street performers. This area is a hub of Amsterdam nightlife and dining.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Café Loetje or Scandinavian Embassy near the Museumplein area — try Dutch poffertjes (mini pancakes) or a classic Dutch breakfast with cheese and cold cuts (~€10–15).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Rijksmuseum's café or a picnic from a nearby Albert Heijn supermarket eaten in Vondelpark (~€8–12). The park is beautiful in May.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Brasserie Keyzer, a historic grand café next to the Concertgebouw — classic Dutch and European cuisine in an elegant but relaxed setting. Budget ~€28–38 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Museum Saturday can be busy — arriving at opening is strongly recommended for both museums. Consider the Museumkaart (Museum Card, ~€65) if planning to visit 5+ museums during your trip, as it pays for itself quickly. Vondelpark is lovely in May and perfect for a midday rest between museum visits.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour: This is the most emotionally significant experience of the trip. Pre-booking is essential (tickets often sell out weeks in advance, ~€16 per person). Time slots begin at 9:00 AM. Walk through the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid during WWII. Allow 1.5–2 hours. The house is located in the Jordaan district, very close to most canal house accommodations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jordaan Neighborhood Walking Tour & Dutch Food Tasting: After a reflective morning, transition into a guided Jordaan Walking Tour with Dutch food tasting (~€30–40 per person, 2.5 hours). Explore hidden courtyards (hofjes), local markets, quirky galleries, and taste Dutch specialties like bitterballen, herring, stroopwafels, and Dutch cheese. This tour perfectly balances the weight of the morning with cultural delight.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Canal Walk & Brown Café Experience: Take a self-guided sunset stroll along the Prinsengracht and Brouwersgracht canals — among Amsterdam's most photogenic spots. End the evening at a traditional Dutch 'brown café' (bruine kroeg) for local beers and bar snacks.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or at Buffet van Odette, a charming café near the Anne Frank House — fresh pastries, eggs, and good coffee (~€10–14).
meals.lunch: Included as part of the Jordaan food tasting tour, or supplement with a herring sandwich (broodje haring) from a street stall — a must-try Amsterdam experience (~€4–6).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Toscanini, a beloved Italian restaurant in the Jordaan known for its fresh pasta and warm atmosphere. Budget ~€25–35 per person. Reserve ahead as it's popular on Sundays.

day_by_day.notes: The Anne Frank House is deeply moving — take time to process the experience before rushing into the next activity. The food tour in the afternoon provides a welcome emotional counterbalance. Sunday markets (like the Noordermarkt organic market, open until 3 PM) are worth a quick browse if timing allows before the walking tour.

day_by_day.morning: Amsterdam Historical Museum & De Pijp District: Visit the Amsterdam Museum (Amsterdams Historisch Museum) in the city center to deepen your understanding of the city's 700-year history — from medieval trading port to Golden Age powerhouse (~€15 per person, allow 1.5–2 hours). Then take Tram 24 south to the vibrant De Pijp neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Albert Cuyp Market & De Pijp Exploration: Stroll through the Albert Cuyp Market (open Mon–Sat, closes ~5 PM) — Amsterdam's largest and most colorful street market, stretching nearly a kilometer with fresh produce, flowers, clothing, and street food. Explore De Pijp's independent boutiques, vintage shops, and multicultural street scene. Visit the Heineken Experience (~€23) if interested in Dutch brewing history (located right in De Pijp).
day_by_day.evening: Classical Music or Jazz: Check the schedule at the Concertgebouw (world-class concert hall — free lunchtime concerts on Wednesdays, evening tickets ~€30–60) or catch live jazz at Bimhuis or Bourbon Street Jazz & Blues Club for a more casual evening. Amsterdam's music scene is excellent in May.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Café Brecht or a local bakery near the hotel — fresh bread, Dutch cheese, and coffee (~€8–12).
meals.lunch: Street food lunch at the Albert Cuyp Market — try a stroopwafel fresh off the iron, Dutch fries (patat) with mayo, or a fresh herring. Budget ~€8–12 for a satisfying market lunch.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Brouwerij 't IJ, a craft brewery inside a historic windmill on the eastern edge of the city (short tram ride) — enjoy local craft beers paired with hearty Dutch bar food. Budget ~€18–25 per person. Alternatively, dine at a De Pijp restaurant like Café Buurman & Buurman (~€22–30).

day_by_day.notes: Monday is a good day for markets and neighborhoods as some smaller museums may be closed. The Albert Cuyp Market is a true local experience and not overly touristy. If the Heineken Experience feels too commercial, skip it and spend more time exploring De Pijp's independent café culture instead.

day_by_day.morning: Begijnhof & Amsterdam's Hidden Courtyards: Start the final morning with a visit to the Begijnhof, one of Amsterdam's oldest and most serene hidden courtyards (free entry, opens 9 AM). Admire the medieval chapel and centuries-old houses. Nearby, explore the Spui square and browse the Friday book market (check if open). Walk along the Singel canal — Amsterdam's innermost canal ring — for a peaceful final morning stroll.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rembrandt House Museum & Jewish Historical Museum: Visit the Museum Het Rembrandthuis (Rembrandt's House, ~€16) in the old Jewish quarter to see the master's reconstructed studio and original etchings. Nearby, the Jewish Historical Museum and the Portuguese Synagogue offer powerful insights into Amsterdam's rich Jewish heritage (~€17 combined). The area around Waterlooplein also has a daily flea market worth browsing.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Canal-Side Drinks: Spend your final evening with a special dinner at a canal-side restaurant, then take a leisurely evening walk along the illuminated canals — Amsterdam's canal lighting at dusk is magical. End with a drink at a rooftop bar or a classic brown café to toast the trip.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a proper Dutch breakfast at Winkel 43 in the Jordaan — famous for its apple pie but also serves excellent breakfast. Arrive early as queues form (~€10–15).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Brasserie Harkema near the Spui — a stylish brasserie in a converted tobacco factory with great value lunch menus (~€14–18 for a two-course lunch).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Restaurant Greetje, Amsterdam's finest Dutch cuisine restaurant, celebrating traditional Dutch recipes with modern flair. Budget ~€40–55 per person — a splurge worth it for the last night. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Leave the final afternoon flexible depending on energy levels and any missed experiences from earlier days. If departing early the next morning, pack bags the night before and confirm your Schiphol transport plan — the train from Amsterdam Centraal runs frequently and takes ~17 minutes. The Amsterdam Card or GVB multi-day transit pass (~€17 for 24h, ~€26 for 48h, ~€34 for 72h) is recommended throughout the trip for unlimited tram, bus, and metro travel.

trip_options.title: Premium Amsterdam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Amsterdam Airport Schiphol at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private chauffeur transfer arranged from Schiphol to Canal House Amsterdam. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your luxury canal-view suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Canal Boat Tour: After settling in, embark on a private guided canal boat tour of Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed canal ring. Glide past 17th-century merchant houses, historic bridges, and the iconic Grachtengordel at a leisurely pace. Your private captain will narrate the city's Golden Age history as you sip champagne on board.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Herengracht and Keizersgracht canals at dusk as the city lights begin to reflect on the water. Enjoy a welcome dinner at a top Amsterdam restaurant to begin your luxury stay in style.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at Canal House Amsterdam upon check-in, or a quick refined bite at Breitner Restaurant near the hotel.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Vinkeles (inside The Dylan Hotel) — a Michelin-starred gem serving contemporary French-Dutch cuisine in a stunning 18th-century bakery setting. Reserve the tasting menu with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance with your hotel concierge. Request an early check-in if possible given the 13:00 arrival. The canal boat tour can be booked as a private charter departing from the hotel's canal-side dock area for maximum convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit: Begin your cultural immersion with a private guided tour of the Rijksmuseum, the Netherlands' premier museum. Marvel at Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch,' Vermeer's 'The Milkmaid,' and an extraordinary collection of Dutch Golden Age masterpieces. A private guide will provide deep historical and artistic context unavailable on a standard visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum: A short walk from the Rijksmuseum, immerse yourself in the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's works. See 'Sunflowers,' 'The Bedroom,' and over 200 paintings tracing his turbulent artistic evolution. Book a premium timed-entry or private curator-led experience to avoid crowds and gain exclusive insights.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the elegant Museum Quarter neighbourhood on foot before heading to dinner. Optionally visit the Concertgebouw for an evening concert if the schedule aligns — one of the world's finest concert halls with near-perfect acoustics.

meals.breakfast: Lavish breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam's dining room — expect freshly baked pastries, Dutch cheeses, smoked salmon, and artisan coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Rijksmuseum's Grand Café or the elegant Cobra Café on Museumplein — relaxed but refined, with Dutch-inspired seasonal dishes.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ciel Bleu Restaurant on the 23rd floor of Hotel Okura — two Michelin stars, panoramic Amsterdam skyline views, and an exceptional contemporary European tasting menu with sommelier-curated wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book timed-entry tickets for both the Rijksmuseum and Van Gogh Museum well in advance — both are extremely popular, especially on weekends. Consider a combined private art guide for both museums for a seamless experience.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour: A profoundly moving and historically essential experience. Walk through the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family sheltered during World War II. The museum offers an intimate and deeply human connection to one of history's darkest chapters. Book a premium early-access or private guided slot to experience the space with fewer visitors and maximum reflection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jordaan Neighborhood Walking Tour & Dutch Food Tasting: After the emotional weight of the Anne Frank House, transition into Amsterdam's most charming and picturesque neighbourhood. Join a private guided walking tour of the Jordaan, exploring hidden courtyards (hofjes), independent art galleries, and artisan boutiques. Enjoy a curated Dutch food tasting along the way — local cheeses, stroopwafels, bitterballen, and Dutch gin (jenever) at a traditional proeflokaal (tasting house).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the boutique galleries and antique shops along Elandsgracht and Nieuwe Spiegelstraat at leisure. Enjoy a pre-dinner drink at a sophisticated canal-side bar before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Canvas on the 7th floor of Volkshotel for a change of scenery — stylish setting with city views, excellent coffee, and a creative brunch menu. Alternatively, breakfast in-hotel.
meals.lunch: During the Jordaan food tasting tour — a curated selection of Dutch artisan bites, local cheeses, and jenever tastings at traditional spots like Café 't Smalle or Proeflokaal Wynand Fockink.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Breda Restaurant in the Jordaan — a celebrated neighbourhood gem offering inventive modern European cuisine with an intimate atmosphere and an outstanding natural wine list.

day_by_day.notes: The Anne Frank House requires advance booking — slots sell out weeks ahead, especially on weekends. Request the first available morning slot for the quietest experience. The Jordaan tour pairs beautifully with the afternoon, as the neighbourhood is just steps from the Anne Frank House.

day_by_day.morning: Private History & Architecture Walking Tour of Amsterdam's Canal Ring: Engage a specialist private guide for an in-depth exploration of the Grachtengordel — the UNESCO World Heritage canal belt. Discover the stories behind the grand merchant houses, the Dutch East India Company (VOC) legacy, hidden churches, and the architectural genius of 17th-century Amsterdam. Visit the Royal Palace on Dam Square and explore the historic heart of the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Amsterdam Museum (or the newly renovated Amsterdam City Archives) for a deeper dive into the city's rich history, followed by a leisurely browse through the prestigious antique dealers and art galleries along Nieuwe Spiegelstraat — one of Europe's finest antique shopping streets. Consider visiting the Foam Photography Museum or the Hermitage Amsterdam for additional cultural enrichment.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset canal cruise: Board a beautifully appointed private electric boat for a golden-hour cruise through the lesser-known canals of Amsterdam. Sip Dutch craft beer or sparkling wine as the city glows in the evening light. Return to the hotel to freshen up before dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam — take your time over a full Dutch breakfast with freshly squeezed juices, local cold cuts, and pastries.
meals.lunch: Lunch at De Silveren Spiegel — one of Amsterdam's oldest and most historic restaurants, serving traditional Dutch cuisine in a stunning 1614 canal house near Dam Square.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Spectrum Restaurant inside the W Amsterdam hotel — a bold, design-forward Michelin-starred restaurant offering a theatrical tasting menu that celebrates Dutch ingredients with global technique. Exceptional cocktail bar on-site for a nightcap.

day_by_day.notes: The private sunset canal cruise can be arranged through your hotel concierge — electric 'sloep' boats are quiet, eco-friendly, and ideal for intimate evening cruises. Bring a light jacket as canal evenings can be cool in May.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning at Canal House Amsterdam — enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast and take time to relax in the hotel's elegant garden or lounge. Optionally, visit the nearby Westerkerk (Western Church) — Amsterdam's largest 17th-century church and the burial place of Rembrandt — for a quiet, reflective cultural moment before departure preparations begin.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final exploration: Visit the Moco Museum (Modern Contemporary Museum) near Museumplein for a curated collection of Banksy works and contemporary art — a stylish and thought-provoking contrast to the classical museums visited earlier in the trip. Alternatively, indulge in a luxury shopping session along P.C. Hooftstraat — Amsterdam's premier luxury retail street — featuring Hermès, Louis Vuitton, Chanel, and top Dutch designers.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a celebrated Amsterdam restaurant, followed by a final evening stroll along the illuminated canals. Private chauffeur transfer to Schiphol Airport arranged as needed.

meals.breakfast: Extended, leisurely in-hotel breakfast — savour the last morning in your canal-view suite with a full spread and excellent coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ron Gastrobar — a relaxed yet refined concept by Michelin-starred chef Ron Blaauw, offering accessible luxury with creative small plates and outstanding cocktails in a beautiful setting.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Amstel InterContinental's La Rive — a legendary Amsterdam institution with two Michelin stars, French-Dutch haute cuisine, and stunning riverside terrace views. An unforgettable conclusion to a premium Amsterdam experience.
